headline: Saxony-Anhalt is set to seat Germany’s first AfD parliament president; the Mecca pact sends Turkish and Pakistani troops to Saudi Arabia; Reflection unveils Beam.

stories.title: Saxony-Anhalt is set to elect Germany’s first AfD state parliament president today
facts: The new Magdeburg Landtag meets for its constituent session at 11:00; AfD nominee Tobias Rausch (35, in the Landtag since 2016 and the party’s state general secretary) is all but certain to win.
Arithmetic: AfD 39 seats plus BSW 5 makes 44, enough for a majority; CDU, SPD, Linke and Greens together hold 39. CDU leader and caretaker premier Sven Schulze tells his MPs to abstain.

Wagenknecht to dpa: “Das BSW beendet die Brandmauer-Idiotie!” — the strongest group should get the post “at 44 percent of the vote”; she calls Göring comparisons from SPD, Greens and Linke a trivialisation of Nazism.
Critics cite Rausch’s past calls to order, his double role as party general secretary, and the AfD nepotism affair; Rausch promises to be “hart in der Sache, aber fair in der Person”.
With BSW backing, the AfD also won a new seating plan: its 39 MPs now sit in the centre of the chamber. The premier vote follows in December, where the CDU again rules out backing Ulrich Siegmund.
stories.whyItMatters: First time the AfD would hold a Land’s top parliamentary office, and the first real test of whether AfD and BSW can deliver votes together.

stories.title: Turkey and Pakistan send forces to Saudi Arabia as the Mecca defence pact is triggered for the first time
facts: Emergency meeting of defence and foreign ministers in Riyadh on Monday: the three states “activate collective deterrence measures” and will rapidly deploy “agreed military forces and capabilities” to the kingdom (joint statement via Pakistan’s foreign ministry).
The pact, signed 7 August, treats an attack on one as an attack on all; this is its first invocation. Trigger: last week’s Houthi strike on a Medina substation that powers the Prophet’s Mosque.
Riyadh was shaken by loud explosions on Monday evening (AFP); the Houthis claim hits on King Khalid airport and Aramco’s Rabigh refinery — not confirmed by Riyadh.

Material update to last night’s Bab el-Mandeb card: Yemeni government forces now claim to have retaken Mocha and launched a “strategic offensive” on Sanaa; the Houthis deny Mocha fell and Al Jazeera can’t verify either side.
stories.whyItMatters: Turns a Saudi–Houthi war into a three-country military commitment — and pulls Ankara and Islamabad out of their mediator roles in the wider Iran war.

image.alt: Turkiye, Pakistan agree Saudi Arabia military deployment under Mecca pact

stories.title: Reflection unveils Beam, a 501B open-weight model pitched as the West’s answer to Chinese open models
facts: Sparse mixture-of-experts: 501B total / 23B active parameters, pretrained on 23.8T tokens, text-only, 1M-token context (TechCrunch).
RL run: 10.5K Nvidia GB300 GPUs for four weeks, 100M+ rollouts, ~1.3bn sandboxes — Reflection calls it one of the largest RL runs by any open lab.

Claims: reasoning on par with Z.ai’s GLM-5.2 at 3–4× less inference compute, approaching Qwen 3.8-Max on coding/agentic; it concedes Kimi K3 is still ahead on raw capability. Not independently verified.
Still in red-teaming: weights, technical report and model card are due “later this month”; early-access sign-up now.
Backers include Nvidia, Sequoia and Lightspeed (~$4.7bn raised, $25bn pre-money per PitchBook); it pitches “AI factories” to enterprises and sovereign buyers.
stories.whyItMatters: The best-funded US bet on open weights finally has a model; the real test is when the weights and report land.

stories.title: FBI removes an Accenture contractor over an unpatched system behind its staff-data breach
facts: FBI cyber chief Brett Leatherman: the breach came from “a security failure of a platform managed by a third-party organisation” after a contractor failed to apply a patch “explicitly issued” for it; the contractor was removed on 5 October.
Two sources told Reuters the platform was Oracle’s PeopleSoft HR system and the third party was Accenture; the FBI named neither.
ShinyHunters said on 22 September it had breached the FBI’s job site and stolen data on current and former employees; thousands of staff had sensitive details exposed.
Accenture said it is “proud to support the mission of the FBI” and didn’t answer questions on the patch.

image.alt: The hacking group ShinyHunters said on Sept 22 that they had breached the FBI, stealing data on a large number of current and former FBI employees.

stories.title: Ex-lab researchers tell New York City Council AI companies are “extremely reckless”
facts: Hearing called by Council Speaker Julie Menin as the city weighs its own AI guardrails; Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta sent policy staff, appearing virtually.
Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon: “the majority of the code is now written by AI, and people do not check it that carefully anymore.”
Ex-DeepMind researcher Alex Turner put AI-takeover odds at “roughly one in three”; Daniel Kokotajlo (AI Futures Project) warned labs could use control of AI to become “dictators or oligarchs”.

stories.title: Verfassungsschutz: Iran is ramping up shopping for missile tech in Germany; Russian sabotage risk rising
facts: New BfV situation report on counter-espionage (reported by WELT): “persistently high” Iranian procurement for its launcher and missile programmes, “with a rising tendency”.
Rationale: after the war since February 2026, Iran is expected to refill and expand its arsenals and rebuild destroyed plants — and still depends on Western tech where Germany is a leading maker.
UN and EU sanctions (back since September 2025) push Iranian buyers toward “concealing and conspiratorial” behaviour.
Same report warns of a “further falling threshold” for Russian sabotage acts that accept collateral damage — following Monday’s BND warning.

stories.title: Conscientious-objector applications triple in Germany
facts: 12,102 applications Jan–Aug 2026 at the federal family/civil-society office, vs 3,879 in all of 2025 (Funke/RND, via SPIEGEL).
End of June the count was 5,862 — it has roughly doubled in two months.
Drivers named: the tense security situation and the new Wehrdienst law; many applications are being sent back unprocessed.

stories.title: netzpolitik.org: ad-tech location data tracks visitors to German churches, mosques and synagogues
facts: More than one million phone location points at Christian, Muslim and Jewish sites in Germany — found in free preview data from data brokers.
Movement profiles are accurate to a few metres and lead to home addresses; the team traced one Göttingen churchgoer to a named household.
Also visible: regular visitors to the German Bishops’ Conference, the EKD headquarters and Jewish community centres and schools; experts warn of a risk for religiously motivated violence.

stories.title: Trump opens tax-free “red dye” farm diesel to all drivers
facts: Executive order signed Monday at a Nebraska rally: waives the off-road requirement so anyone can buy dyed, excise-tax-exempt diesel “for any reason”.
Transportation, Agriculture, Defense and Treasury are told to widen access, and states are encouraged to suspend their diesel taxes (White House fact sheet).
Trump says truckers save >$100 per fill-up; diesel prices have spiked because of the Iran war, and fuel costs are a top midterm issue.

image.alt: New York state declares measles disaster amid resurgence of disease in US

facts.text: Trump approved Hegseth’s recommendation of death by Army firing squad for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan (13 killed in 2009); he’d be the first US soldier executed by the military in 60+ years.
New York declares a measles disaster emergency through 4 Nov: 108 cases this year, 92 since mid-July in under-vaccinated rural communities; more staff may now give MMR shots.
Guardian analysis: over 176,000 tonnes of mostly diesel left South Korean ports for Russia’s far east in July–August on seven tankers, three of them under UK/EU sanctions.
ChatGPT is putting real New Yorker cartoonists’ signatures on AI cartoons — Nieman Lab documented 15+ artists, including Brendan Loper, whose fake “BLOPER” cartoon went viral.

facts.text: Vite shipped five patch lines overnight (8.3.3, 8.2.4, 8.1.6, 7.3.7, 6.4.4) with dev-server hardening: `fs.serve` now checked for `?vite-wasm-instance`, and safe-module tracking stores ids instead of URLs. No advisory published yet — worth updating.
Gleam 1.19 stops generating Erlang source: the rewritten backend emits Erlang abstract forms, for faster builds and BEAM stack traces that point at the real Gleam lines.
vx-underground says GitHub banned it and wiped its entire malware source-code collection.
OpenAI had a rough night: several incidents, the latest hitting ChatGPT conversations, image generation, Spaces/Pages, API rehydration and Dots; all now marked resolved.

Vals AI: a team of Claude Opus 5.5 agents proposed two room-temperature magnet candidates for spintronic memory — zero net magnetism yet spin-sorting; one new, one first made in 1999; calculations and code are published, but nothing has been tested in a lab yet (HN front page).
SvelteKit merged #17325: +server handlers now emit a tracing span when tracing is enabled.
